title: Replace CPT meta UI with repeatable field builder
description: Turn the CPT form into a clearer post type builder with dynamically repeatable fields and taxonomies, keeping advanced registration settings present but not dominant.
objective: Make CPT creation feel like a simpler JetEngine workflow: define the post type, add as many fields as needed through an add-row control, and expose common field types without overwhelming the first view.
expected_outputs: CPT admin uses Post Types naming instead of vague content-model wording.
Meta fields and taxonomies use add/remove repeaters instead of fixed blank row blocks.
Common field types include text, textarea, number, URL, email, date/time variants, checkbox, select, radio, color, image URL, and gallery URLs.
Advanced WordPress registration options are collapsed away from the main path.
Server-side sanitization and safety caps remain enforced.
acceptance_criteria: A new CPT form can add multiple meta fields from the browser without predefined row count limits.
Existing saved fields still render and save through the same option schema.
Blank repeater rows are ignored server-side.
Meta field type allowlist and sanitization cover every exposed field type.
State-changing saves keep manage_options and nonce checks.
verification: WP-CLI option contract smoke saves a CPT with at least three meta fields.
Browser smoke checks the add-field button creates additional inputs without overflow.
MCP validate_task for TASK-015 returned valid.
WP-CLI option contract smoke saved a CPT with three meta fields.
Browser smoke changed field rows from 1 to 3 and taxonomy rows from 0 to 1.

budgets.scope_budget: CPT admin UX and supported field types only
budgets.validation_budget: MCP plus WP-CLI smoke plus browser smoke

risks: The UI can say unlimited while the server must still cap payload size for safety; copy should avoid promising literal infinity.
Adding unsupported JetEngine-like types would be worse than a simpler honest type set.
Changing saved option keys would break existing definitions, so the schema must remain compatible.
